questions.q: The mass of zinc produced by the electrolysis of zinc sulphate solution with a steady current of $0 . 015A$ for $15$ minutes is _ ___ \times {10}^{- 4}g$. (Atomic mass of zinc $= 65 . 4amu )
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Given, t = $15$min

${Zn}^{+ 2} + 2e^{-} ⟶ Zn$

Quantity of charge passed (Q) =Current in amperes ×Time in seconds.
=$( 0 . 015A ) \times ( 15 \times 60 ) s = 13 . 5C$

Gram equivalent mass of zinc = $\dfrac{65 . 4}{2} = 32 . 7$g
Now, $96500$ C of charge deposit zinc =$32 . 7$ g
$13 . 5$ C charge will deposit zinc = $\dfrac{( 32 . 7g )}{( 96500C )} \times ( 13 . 5C ) = 4 . 57 \times {10}^{- 3}g$

$= 45 . 75 \times {10}^{- 4}gm$

Standard electrode potential is a measurement of the potential for equilibrium. There is a potential difference between the electrode and the electrolyte called the potential of the electrode. ${E}_{1}^{0} + 2{E}_{2}^{0} = 3{E}_{3}^{0}$
${E}_{1}^{0} = 3{E}_{3}^{0} - 2{E}_{2}^{0}$

$= 3 ( - 0 . 036 ) - 2 ( - 0 . 44 )$
$= + 0 . 772V$
${E}_{cell }^{0} = {E}_{{Fe}^{3 +} / {Fe}^{2 +}}^{0} + {E}_{I^{-} / {I}_{2}}^{0} = 0 . 233$
${Δ}_{r}G^{0} = - 2 \times 96 . 5 \times 0 . 233 = - 45kJ$

questions.q:
The number of correct statements from the following is...........
A.& ${E}_{cell}$~is an intensive parameter
B. A~negative~$E^{o}$~means that the redox couple is a stronger reducing agent than the~$H^{+} / {H}_{2}$& couple.
C. The amount of electricity required for oxidation or reduction depends on the stoichiometry of the electrode reaction.
D. The amount of chemical reaction which occurs at any electrode during electrolysis by a current is proportional to the quantity of electricity passed through the electrolyte.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
An intensive property is a bulk property, meaning that it is a physical property of a system that does not depend on the system size or the amount of material in the system.

$\Delta G = - {nFE}_{cell} $

The~$∆ G$~in the above equation is an extensive property,~${E}_{cell}$~is an intensive property.~A negative $E^{o}$means that the redox couple is a stronger reducing agent than the~$H^{+} / {H}_{2}$couple.& The amount of electricity required for oxidation or reduction depends on the stoichiometry of the electrode reaction.& The amount of chemical reaction which occurs at any electrode during electrolysis by a current is proportional to the quantity of electricity passed through the electrolyte.

questions.q:
$What would be the electrode potential for the given half-cell reaction at $pH = 5 ? _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ .$
$2{H}_{2}O \to {O}_{2} + 4\overset{⊕}{\text{H}} + 4e^{-}; {E}_{red}^{0} = 1.23V$
\left(R = 8.314J{mol}^{- 1}K^{- 1}; Temp = 298K; oxygenunderstandard . atm . pressureof1bar\right)$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
On applyinf Nernst equation-

$E = E ° - \dfrac{0 . 0591}{n}logQE = - 1 .23 - \dfrac{0 .0591}{4}log{[ H^{+} ]}^{4}$
$= 1.23 + 0.0591 \times pH = - 1.23 + 0.0591 \times 5$
$= - 1.23 + 0.2955 = - 0.9345V = - 0.93V$

The Nernst equation defines the relationship between cell potential to standard potential and to the activities of the electrically active (electroactive) species. It relates the effective concentrations (activities) of the components of a cell reaction to the standard cell potential.

The electrode potential of the following half cell at& $298K$

$X\left|X^{2 +}\left(0 . 001M\right) ‖ Y^{2 +}\left(0 . 01M\right)\right|Y$~is~_____~$\times {10}^{- 2}V$ (Nearest integer)

Given : ${E}_{X^{2 +} ∣ X}^{0} = - 2 . 36V$

${E}_{Y^{2 +}Y}^{0} = + 0 . 36V$

$\dfrac{2 . 303RT}{F} = 0 . 06V$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
$The net cell reaction can be written as follows,

$X + Y^{2 +} \to Y + X^{2 +}$

${E}_{cell}^{0} = {E}_{cathode}^{0} - {E}_{anode}^{0}$(Both are SRP values)

${E}_{Cell}^{0} = 0 . 36 - \left(- 2 . 36\right) = 2 . 72V$

Now, the Nernst equation is,

${E}_{cell} = {E}_{cell}^{0} - \dfrac{0 . 06}{n}log \left[X^{2 +}\$right]\left[Y^{2 +}\right]$

$n =$The number of electrons involved in the net reaction.

${E}_{Cell} = 2 . 72 - $\dfrac{0 . 0$0$006}{2}log\dfrac{0 . 001}{0 . 01}$

$= 2 . 72 + 0 . 03 = 2 . 75V$

$= 275 \times {10}^{- 2}V$

$

(Given : ${E}_{{Cu}^{2 +} / Cu}^{o} = 0 . 34V$ and \dfrac{2 . 303RT}{F} =$0 . 06V$)

$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
$Anode& $⇒ {H}_{2}\left(g\right) ⟶ 2H^{+} \left(aq\right) + 2e^{-}$

Cathode~$⇒ {Cu}^{2 +}\left(aq\right) + 2e^{-} ⟶ Cu\left(s\right)$

Overall~$⇒ \$mathop{{H}_{2}\left($q\right) + {Cu}^{2 $+}\left($aq\right) ⟶ $2H^{+}\left($aq\right) + $Cu\left($s\right)}_{¯}$

${E}_{cell}^{°} = {E}_{{Cu}^{2 +} Cu}^{°} - {E}_{H^{+} {H}_{2}}^{°} = 0 . 34V$

${E}_{cell} = {E}_{cell}^{°} - \dfrac{0 . 06}{2}log \left[$H^{+}\right]2 \left[{Cu}^{2 +}\right]$

$0 . 576 = 0 . 34 + 0 . 03 \left[-log \left[$H^{+}\right]2 + $log\left[{Cu}^{2 +}\right]\right

$0 . 576 = 0 . 34 + 0 . 03 \left[$2pH + log \left[{Cu}^{2 +}\right]\right]

$0 . 236 = 0 . 03 \left[2pH - 2\right]$

$7 . 866 = 2pH - 2$

$pH = 4 . 93 \approx 5$

$
